cognate: ON bíta ~ Skt bhid- ~ Lat. findo (*bʰeyd- 'split'); ON hjarta ~ Skt hṛdaya ~ Lat. cor (*ḱerd-)
drift_or_renewal: ON bíta has drifted from 'split' to 'bite (of a weapon)'; Skt and Latin keep 'split'
shared_syntax: Skt: weapon splits the heart (bibheda hṛdayam / bhinna-hṛdaya-); ON: iron 'bit' at the heart (hjarta et næsta, dative), so the heart is the goal of the verb rather than its direct object
context: mortal missile wound in battle: Þormóðr's verse on the arrow that bit closest to his heart; MBh warrior struck by an arrow in the chest, 'split-hearted', vomits blood and falls. bhid- + hṛdaya is a stock epic formula (dozens of hits) and already Atharvan (AVP 12.21 against rivals); Plautus has cor ... finditur of grief

near_miss.lead: killing of kin listed as mother/brother/sister (ON moðor broðor ... systur; AV hata mātā ... hata bhrātā hata svasā)
near_miss.why_not: exact cognate kin terms, but kin lists are generic; ON is a law on kin-slaying (óbótamaðr), AV a charm destroying a worm's family: different function, verbs not cognate (drepa vs han-)

near_miss.lead: merism 'day and night' (ON dag oc nótt ~ νυκτός τε καὶ ἤματος)
near_miss.why_not: only nótt ~ νύξ cognate, day-word renewed; the merism is universal and the contexts (vigilance in arms vs paths of night and day) differ

near_miss.lead: stranger asked name, kin and homeland (nafn ... kynferð ... landzmaðr ~ γένος ... πάτρης ... οὔνομα)
near_miss.why_not: universal type scene; in Herodotus 'name' is the fatherland's name, not the man's; land vs πάτρη renewed; nothing beyond generic

near_miss.lead: binding/fetter (festr man slitna) vs bound in a net of arrows (baddhāḥ śara jālena)
near_miss.why_not: no shared wording: breaking of a fetter vs being bound; roots not shared in collocation
Thucydides partner irrelevant (φείδομαι mapped to *bʰeyd-); no Greek bhid+heart parallel found (one late Plutarch hit only)

error.correct_reading: hrár 'raw' (n. sg. hrátt, agreeing with hold), < *kreuh₂- (Skt kravís, Gk κρέας, Lat. cruor)
error.evidence: 'hrátt gafz hold at slíta hrafni' = raw flesh was given the raven to tear; long á, not pret. hratt of hrinda
idiom 'þá rann á hann svefn' = sleep came over him
'отверзета ся очи ваю' (Gen 3.5) = your eyes will be opened
'Sal ser hon standa ... gulli þaktan a gimle' = she sees a hall standing; also in 20v:19
'norðr horfa dyrr' = its doors face north (Vǫluspá, Náströnd hall)
